__baseline_prompt__.text: A folk-horror photograph of a fictional adult woman returning from an English midwinter orchard wassail, a rural communal custom becoming unsettling at a household threshold. Use the supplied photograph as the face-and-hair appearance reference: her softly rounded facial outline, large dark brown eyes, small straight nose, soft pink lips, chin-length dark brown bob and separated fringe remain recognizable. She has just crossed the worn stone step of a small orchard cottage but has paused with the oak door open behind her, listening toward the trees rather than greeting the camera. Both her hands cup opposite sides of one broad wooden drinking bowl at waist height, her fingers following its lower curve and its open rim fully visible. Cider trembles close to the rim. Her elbows rest naturally near her ribs and her weight settles on the inside foot. A damp wool dress and open knitted cardigan hold the ordinary warmth of someone expected home; a loose strand of hair against her cheek and quiet parted lips give her a restrained, intimate presence. Beyond the open door, bare apple branches carry a few rain-dark ribbons tied directly around the wood, and two distant torch-bearing figures stand still between the rows. A ribbon end is caught inside the doorway while the rest runs back outside, as though the orchard has followed her home. Warm hearth light grazes her face and the bowl; blue winter dusk keeps the orchard legible. Make the threshold, bowl and nearest ribboned branch read together in a medium-wide photograph taken from inside the cottage, with the woman slightly off center and the exterior visible beside her. The unease comes from the stopped return and the waiting custom, while wet stone, cider and wool retain tactile photographic credibility.
